The journey is on hold. Take a breath, then turn toward the next signal on your radar.

FLIGHT MANUAL / KEEP THE RADAR IN SIGHT

Light arrows, all around.

Forward motion follows the rail. Move the dragon to evade incoming shells, while aiming independently. Your camera turns in four directions; turning does not change the route. At the fork, physically steer left or right before the countdown ends.

Choose your weapon.

The rifle fires immediately and destroys orange projectiles, tents, and bonus debris. It is especially effective against small battleships and the transport’s first cannons. The laser remembers up to four locks across camera turns; large targets can take multiple locks. Release a full volley for a score bonus. Rifle fire stops while charging lasers.

Read the circle.

The radar is fixed to the direction of travel. F is forward, B is behind. The pale wedge shows your current view. Orange expanding rings warn that a target is about to shoot. Orange shells can be intercepted or dodged; your dragon’s body, not the reticle, must clear them.

Spend the light.

Kills restore Berserk energy. Activate with at least 10 energy: lasers automatically attack visible enemies, incoming fire dissolves, and you are invulnerable until the meter empties. Camera control remains important. Three optional turquoise memories restore 24 vitality and 22 energy each.

Finish the transport to evolve into Glideling. Replay with six locks from the title screen. Clear, route, and technical points are tallied separately; 80% shot down earns one technical point, 90% earns two. Best scores and evolution are saved locally when the browser permits it.

EMBEDDED DOCUMENTATION / COMPLETION REPORT

Sablewing

The Meccania Passage · Generated September 29, 2026 with GPT-6 Astra Pro. A self-contained, single-level, non-commercial tribute to Panzer Dragoon II Zwei (Sega Saturn). No Sega game data, extracted models, or source recordings are bundled.

Delivery exceptions, not hidden substitutions. Package downloads and binary audio retrieval were unavailable in the build environment. This file therefore uses an original native WebGPU / WebGL2 renderer, not three.js r186, and original synthesized MP3s, not source-game music or sounds. Vite was not available; TypeScript 5.8.3 compiled the source. It is a playable offline adaptation, but it does not meet those specified stack and source-audio requirements.
Launch & compatibility

Save this HTML and open it directly in a modern browser with hardware acceleration. No installation, server, runtime download, CDN, network request, or external asset is required. Choose Begin journey. Click or press a key once to unlock sound; gamepad-only startup may initially be silent under autoplay restrictions. Landscape is recommended on phones. Native WebGPU is tried first; WebGL2 is the automatic fallback. To test WebGL2 explicitly, append #webgl to the local file address. Fullscreen requires browser support and a permitted user gesture.

Settings, route-specific best scores, the Glideling unlock, and a boss-entry checkpoint use localStorage under sablewing-v1. Browsers may restrict storage for local files or private windows; in that case the game still runs with session-only state. A checkpoint retry is marked assisted and never overwrites a clean best score. The fixed 60 Hz simulation is capped at six catch-up steps per frame and rendering interpolates moving actors and projectiles.

Selected source: Episode 2 / Great Canyon

The level inventory follows EnemyZero’s Episode 2 walkthrough, cross-referenced with Jeremy Prusak’s guide. Encounters are procedurally restaged rather than a frame-exact Saturn map reconstruction. The authored route is continuous: a common approach, one complete selected branch, the transport fight, and a forest-bound ending.

Second graphics pass — Render the air

Build date: 29 September 2026. Model: GPT-6 Astra Pro. This pass changes the environment and its response to movement. The level routes, encounters, damage, weapons, score rules, and save key are retained.

ChangeWhere it appears
Height-dependent airAnalytic height haze makes low ground more dense than high air. Directional scattering warms the view toward the sun. Ground haze breaks into drifting sheets.
Depth and lightClouds move above the canyon. Light changes across the rock. Soft particles read the solid-scene depth and fade at intersections instead of forming hard circles.
Wind and small detailSuspended dust, roadside grass, worn cloth, and the rider's cape use a common wind signal. Shale and damaged posts give the ground more scale.
Movement through the airFoot strikes lift small dust clouds. Wingtip wakes stay in world space. Ship exhaust drifts, expands, and darkens as damage increases.
Combat responseBlasts push nearby dust away, add expanding pressure trails, and light the air briefly. Carrier exhaust and recent blasts can produce local heat shimmer.
Surface and combat clarityRock has fine layers and grain. Ground normals are smooth. Soft flashes replace the hard round sparks. The camera sits slightly farther back and aims lower to keep the dragon in view.
Route characterThe fortress road has low dust and windblown sand. The upper route has thin wakes and cloud banks below flight height. The forest ending moves toward cool mist.

Controls: Open Options for Air detail: Full, Light, or Off. Light shafts and Local heat shimmer are separate switches. Both are off by default. Full respects the active Auto, Balanced, or High preset. No combat rule changes with these settings. Off removes the added height haze and transient air effects. The new sky, surface lighting, and wind-driven cloth remain.

Rendering notes: Solid geometry renders to color and depth. Alpha cards render in a separate pass and sample that depth. Soft alpha edges and back-to-front card sorting replace the old dust spheres. The optional light shafts use sampled analytic light masks, not a shadow-map volume simulation. Heat shimmer is limited to projected heat sources and rejects large depth changes. The contact shadows remain approximations.

Asset notes: All new geometry, shaders, cloud fields, and particles are generated in the file. No image, font, sound, library, or network resource was added. The 14 original synthesized MP3 assets are unchanged. There are still no authentic Sega recordings or three.js/Vite dependencies.

Performance limits: Balanced permits 170 ambient motes and 52 transient air puffs. High permits 330 motes and 96 puffs. Light reduces the mote limit and air strength. Each wing wake holds at most 24 points. At most five pressure waves and four heat sources are active. Unused terrain buffers are released. Auto still uses measured frame time.

Hub migration: Port the native GLSL/WGSL material functions to TSL node materials. Port the separate depth-reading alpha pass and the depth-aware heat pass through the hub renderer. Preserve world-space particle state, the fixed-step update, and the interpolated draw. The atmosphere module currently builds meshes through the existing custom geometry interface. It must use hub mesh adapters after migration.

The intact HTML was loaded into a browser page. The environment blocked direct local-file navigation. No game HTTP or HTTPS requests occurred.

Encounter-by-encounter source map

Times are elapsed from launch. The common opening is followed by one selected branch. Facing is relative to the direction of travel; waves overlap. Source-derived encounters use original procedural models and retuned trajectories. Memory pickups are explicitly original additions.

At 3:04 both branches converge on the transport: two belly cannons, three rear guns, then the armored-to-exposed engine heart. Each subsystem must be destroyed; the fight never clears on a timer. Shootable debris follows subsystem destruction and the final explosion.

Original additions & modernization

Independent movement and aiming; fast queued quarter-turns; visible attack windups; touch controls with explicit rifle mode; boss-entry checkpoint and assisted retry; route-choice countdown; three optional healing/energy memories; full-volley and kill-chain bonuses; readable subsystem bars; reduced camera shake option; immediate rifle autofire; score-rank presentation; measured automatic resolution scaling. These are additions, not claims about Saturn content. The source’s radar-driven awareness, hold/sweep/release lock-on rhythm, target-priority choices, and running-to-flight pacing remain the organizing mechanics.

Art is original, procedurally constructed geometry: a plated two-legged dragon and rider, articulated membrane wings, segmented tail, insect burrowers, mounted scouts, armored fighters, small battleships, an original transport silhouette, sandstone cliffs, imperial gates, tents, and alien trees. All lighting, fog, particles, shadows, and animations are generated locally. The second graphics pass adds height-dependent haze, soft world-space dust, coherent wind, cloud layers, moving cloth, wakes, and pressure-driven dust. These are original additions, not recovered Saturn effects.

Intentionally outside this slice

Episodes 1 and 3–7; their bosses and route trees; the original cinematic footage and spoken language; a full campaign save system; later dragon forms beyond Glideling; campaign-specific Pandora’s Box cheats, Zero Space, and historical score tables. No source asset archive or full walkthrough text is redistributed.

Known issues & validation boundaries

Known deviations: the requested three.js 0.186.0 / Vite stack and authentic placeholder audio are absent. The custom renderer is not a disguised three.js implementation. The level is a guide-based reinterpretation, not an exact map or animation remaster. Shadows are projected contact silhouettes, not PCF shadow maps. Native shaders are not TSL.

Performance on a Galaxy S25 or RTX 3060 has not been measured. Auto uses observed frame intervals, and software rendering can be substantially slower. Mobile OS file viewers may preview HTML rather than execute it; an actual browser must open the document. Local-file storage, fullscreen, gamepad availability, and audio autoplay depend on browser policy. Gamepad hardware and real phone touch behavior have not been hardware-certified. The native WebGPU path is implemented but could not be exercised in this browser environment; WebGL2 is the verified rendering path. The embedded browser-test record below distinguishes exercised paths from unverified devices.

First-pass test record — 29 September 2026 (retained). The following tests were recorded for the first delivered file. The new air-pass tests are listed above. TypeScript 5.8.3 strict compilation passed. Browser checks used Chromium 144.0.7559.96 with the SwiftShader software WebGL2 renderer. The document was injected intact into a browser page because this environment's navigation policy blocks opening local-file URLs. No game HTTP/HTTPS requests occurred. This is not a claim that direct file launch, hardware WebGPU, or target-device frame rate was measured.

Engine boundary & hub migration

The TypeScript is split into math/geometry, renderer, engine services, model library, atmosphere, level logic, and UI bootstrap. Game depends on the small Engine service surface: renderer draw/project, input snapshots, audio manifest IDs, settings, lifecycle, and save state. All library-free source modules are embedded below in inert script blocks for inspection.

For the hub, replace SW.Renderer with the hub’s three.js 0.186.0 WebGPURenderer service and convert the native shader pair to node materials / TSL. Replace the matrix and generated-mesh adapters with hub primitives. Preserve async initialization, the loading cover, input edges, and audio gesture unlock. Do not import this custom renderer alongside the hub renderer. The custom rail convention uses +Z forward and a horizontally reflected projection so +X is screen-right in front view; adapt coordinates and winding deliberately to the hub camera rather than copying that projection. No CDN, copied third-party library, external font, or runtime loader is used.

There are no rigid bodies or contact dynamics, so Rapier and WASM are not required by this implementation. Shooter hits use fixed-step swept sphere tests; shards are capped visual particles, not rigid bodies. Projectile collision capacity is always 96 to avoid changing difficulty with graphics quality. Balanced caps cosmetic particles at 180, High at 340. Geometry chunks are discarded and GPU buffers destroyed when they leave the streaming range. High increases resolution, scenery instances, contact shadows, and optional glow sampling; both backends use the same geometry, material math, fog, and animation.

Build tooling used: TypeScript 5.8.3 (--module none --target ES2020 --strict --outFile), Python packaging, and FFmpeg MP3 encoding. Runtime dependencies: none. These tooling substitutions require attention before migration.

Audio manifest & asset credits

All fourteen MP3 assets are embedded in the single audio-manifest JSON block. The audio manager decodes them after first interaction, routes all voices through one master gain, and uses IDs rather than file paths. Replace manifest entries to change assets without changing gameplay. The requested source recordings could not be downloaded from Sounds Resource / Zophar; none is falsely credited as present.
